title: CRLA/212/2002 of JAGDISH PRASAD Vs STATE

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
 Criminal Appeal No. 212 of 2002
Jagdish Prasad ......... Appellant
 versus
State of Uttaranchal .......... Respondent

Ms. Sangeeta Miyan, Amicus Curiae, present for the Appellant.
Mr. M. A. Khan, learned AGA, present for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent.

JUDGMENT
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)
P.W. 3 Suresh Chandra Juyal wrote a complaint
to Naib Tehsildar, Pauri Garhwal on 04.03.1997 against
accused Jagdish Prasad on the selfsame day which was
registered as case crime no. 06/1997 for the offences
punishable under Section 307, 325, 394 and 506 IPC at
10.30 p.m. The alleged incident took place on 04.03.1997 at
05.00 p.m. The distance between the place of incident and
P.S. concerned was 20 Kilometers and hence, there
appeared to be no delay in lodging F.I.R. After the
investigation, a charge sheet for the offences punishable
under Sections 307, 325, and 506 IPC was submitted. No

2
offence under Section 394 IPC was made out. The case was
committed to the Court of Sessions. When the trial
commenced and prosecution opened it's case charge for the
offence punishable under Section 307 IPC was framed
against the accused, who pleaded not guilty and claimed
trial.
2. P.W. 1 Bachhi Ram, P.W. 2 Digambar Prasad,
P.W. 3 Suresh Chandra Juyal, P.W. 4 Dr. Arun Kumar,
P.W. 5 Dr. K.P. Kuniyal and P.W. 6 Ajay Kumar Singh,
Tehsildar were examined on behalf of the prosecution.
Incriminating evidence was put to the accused under
Section 313 Cr.P.C, in which he said that Bachhi Ram
contested the election of Gram Pradhan, he opposed, and
therefore, he (accused) was falsely implicated in the case.
No evidence was given in the evidence. After considering
the evidence on record, learned Sessions Judge, Pauri
Garhwal, convicted accused under Section 307 IPC and was
awarded two years' rigorous imprisonment alongwith a fine
of Rs. 2,000/-, in default of payment of which, he was
required to undergo six months' further rigorous
imprisonment, vide impugned judgment and order dated
24.08.2002. Aggrieved against the impugned judgment and
order, present criminal appeal was preferred.
3. Prosecution led the evidence through P.W. 1. In
his examination-in-chief, he said that he knew the accused,
who was his co-villager. On 04.03.1997, when he was about

3
to reach from Pauri to his village Karakot via Bawali
School, accused met him on his way. He was going on foot
from Bawali to Karakot. Accused caught hold of him, no
sooner he reached near Debridali. It was 05.00 p.m.
Accused snatched Rs. 2572/- from P.W. 1. Accused also
made an attempt to snatch gold ring from his finger. When
he could not snatch golden ring, he gave a blow of stone on
his finger and robbed him of the said ring. Then, the
accused gave a blow of stone on the head of P.W. 1. P.W. 1
sustained injuries on his head. P.W. 1 raised an alarm. P.W.
2 Digambar Prasad, who was working in the adjoining field,
came to save P.W. 1. Two women, who were working
nearby, came to the rescue of P.W. 1. Accused fled away
after threatening the accused with dire consequences. P.W.
2 contacted his house on telephone. P.W. 1 hired a taxi and
went to Bawali. P.W. 1 was taken to hospital, where he was
admitted. He also said that the accused succeeded in
robbing Rs. 2572/= from his pocket because he became
unconscious. Accused Jagdish was inimical to P.W. 1
because P.W. 1 opposed his election as Gram Pradhan of
Gram Sabha. Accused also used to destroy the trees and
steal buffalos.
4. P.W. 3 Suresh Chandra Juyal was the reporter
of the crime, who wrote his complaint (Exhibit Ka-2),
which was addressed to Tehsildar, Pauri. A brief discussion
of the contents of F.I.R. has been enumerated alongwith the

4
statement of injured in the foregoing paragraph of this
judgment. The same need not be repeated.
5. P.W. 2 Digambar Prasad said that his elder
brother Suresh Chandra (P.W. 3) lived in Pauri. Accused
committed crime with his father on 04.03.1997 at around
05.00 p.m. P.W. 2 was irrigating his land. At 05.00 p.m., his
father was coming from Lawari-Sumerpur to his village.
Accused Jagdish Prasad followed him. Accused assaulted
his father, who raised an alarm. P.W. 2 rushed to the scene
of occurrence. Accused fled away. The head and right hand
of his father bled. Accused threatened him with dire
consequences. His father told P.W. 2 that accused looted
Rs. 2572/- and a golden ring. P.W. 2 called the villagers,
who came on the scene of crime. P.W. 2 handed over his
father to the villagers, made a telephone call to his house. A
dandi was brought, in which the injured was taken to
hospital. The cotton muffler was taken by Naib Tehsildar in
his possession, a memo Exhibit Ka-1 whereof was prepared.
The site plan was prepared by Naib Tehsildar at P.W. 2's
pointing.
6. These witnesses were cross examined on behalf
of the accused, but nothing came in their cross examination,
so as to suspect their testimony.
7. The ocular evidence of P.W. 1 and P.W. 2 was
corroborated by P.W. 4 Dr. Arun Kumar, who conducted x-

5
ray of the head and right limb of the injured. P.W. 4 proved
x-ray reports Exhibit Ka-3 and Exhibit Ka-4, which were
prepared by the technician working under him. In the cross
examination, P.W. 4 admitted that there was no bony injury
in the skull. He found fracture in the index finger of the
injured. There was only one fracture in the distal end of
index finger. It is being said at the cost of repetition that no
injury was found on the skull. P.W. 5 Dr. K.P. Kuniyal
proved supplementary report Exhibit Ka-5, which was
based upon the report of the radiologist. P.W. 5 found three
fractures on two fingers of the injured. The injuries were
grievous in nature. P.W. 5 also proved the report Exhibit
Ka-6 prepared by Dr. Nitin Kumar, Anesthetist. Injured
remained admitted in the District Hospital, Pauri, a
certificate Exhibit Ka-7 whereof was issued by P.W. 5.
P.W. 4 & P.W. 5 was cross-examined. Nothing came in
their cross examination to suggest that their reports were
false.
8. P.W. 6 Ajay Kumar Singh, Tehsildar was the
Investigating Officer, who proved complaint Exhibit Ka-2,
on the basis of which chick FIR Exhibit Ka-8 was prepared.
He also proved copy of G.D. Exhibit Ka-9, site plant
Exhibit Ka-10, took the blood stained clothes of the injured
in his possession, prepared memo Exhibit Ka-1, proved
sample seal Exhibit Ka-11 and finally, on being satisfied
that the accused committed the crime, submitted charge
sheet Exhibit Ka-12 against the accused. P.W.3, the

6
informant, was not the eyewitness of the incident. In fact,
his father (injured) came to him at Pauri on 03.03.1997 and
proceeded to his village on the following day. When his
brother P.W. 2 rang him up informing him that Jagdish
assaulted P.W. 1 with stones, then P.W. 3 hired a taxi and
went to Bawali. He got his father admitted in the hospital,
and on the basis of information provided by his father
(injured), he gave the complaint (Exhibit Ka-2) to Naib
Tehsildar.
9. The ocular evidence rendered by P.W. 1 and
P.W. 2 was therefore, corroborated by P.W. 4 and P.W. 5,
which was investigated into by P.W. 6. P.W. 3 set the
criminal law into motion. There was no inconsistency in the
statements of the prosecution witnesses. The prosecution
story is acceptable. Learned Court below has appropriately
dealt with the prosecution evidence and rightly came to the
conclusion that the prosecution version was proved beyond
a shadow of reasonable doubt. There was nothing on record
to suggest the false implication of the accused-appellant,
who was an ex-army man having no previous criminal
history.
10. But the medical evidence does not point out to
the offence punishable under Section 307 I.P.C. P.W. 4 did
not find fracture on the bone of skull of the injured. He even
could not say whether the injured sustained injury on his
head or not? There was sufficient evidence to show that

7
injured sustained fractures on his fingers, as was indicated
by P.W. 4 and P.W. 5 both. Dr. Nitin Kumar, who prepared
medico-legal injury report Exhibit Ka-6 found lacerated
wound on right index finger with fracture of terminal
phalynx; multiple contused abrasion on a right middle
finger and fracture of proximal phalynx; lacerated wound of
2x1 cm. on left side of middle of head; 2x2.5 cm. lacerated
wound (bone deep) on left side of forehead about 20 cm.
above left eyebrow; 4x1 cm. lacerated wound on left side of
middle of head; 2x1 cm. lacerated wound on left side of
back of head and 1x1 cm. lacerated wound on right side of
middle part of head. Injuries no. 1 and 2 were grievous in
nature. The remaining injuries were simple in nature and
were caused by blunt object. P.W. 5 Dr. K.P. Kuniyal found
fracture proximal phalynx middle finger. Only piece of
terminal phalynx and fracture of middle phalynx with
needle in tip index finger was seen. The injuries, thus
sustained were grievous in nature. Dr. Nitin Kumar himself
did not come to prove his report. He was transfered and
therefore, Exhibit Ka-6 was proved by P.W. 5. No medical
officer said that the injuries sustained by the injured were
sufficient, in the ordinary course, to cause the death of
P.W. 1.
11. It is, therefore, held that the offence punishable
under Section 325 IPC, and not the one punishable under
Section 307 IPC is proved against the accused-appellant.

8
12. While the conviction of the accused-appellant is
affirmed, it is inferred that the accused-appellant is held
guilty of and is convicted of the offence punishable under
Section 325 IPC, instead of one punishable under Section
307 IPC. The sentence awarded under Section 307 IPC is
therefore, set aside and the sentence awarded to the
accused-appellant is modified.
13. While convicting the accused-appellant under
Section 325 IPC, he is directed to undergo rigorous
imprisonment for a period of two years alongwith a fine of
Rs. 2000/-, in default of payment of which, he shall further
undergo simple imprisonment for six months.
14. The Criminal Appeal is thus, finally disposed of
with the modification as above.
15. Accused-appellant is on bail. His bail is
cancelled. He is directed to surrender forthwith before the
Court below to serve out the sentence as above.
16. Let a copy of this judgment alongwith lower
court record be sent to the Sessions Judge, Pauri Garhwal
for compliance.
 (U.C.Dhyani,J.)
Dt. July 15, 2013
Kaushal
